governance.title: Radix Governance: proposals, temperature checks and votes
governance.description: Every Radix community proposal and temperature check read from the ledger: status, XRD results, quorum and voting with your Radix Wallet.

governance.hero_subtitle: Every community proposal and temperature check, read straight from the Radix ledger. See how they are going, what was decided and vote with your Radix Wallet.

how_steps.title: 1. Temperature check
how_steps.text: Anyone can raise an idea. The community votes for or against to gauge support before going further.

how_steps.title: 2. Formal proposal
how_steps.text: If the temperature check passes, it becomes a formal proposal with its ballot options, its quorum and the share it needs to pass.

how_steps.title: 3. Result
how_steps.text: Each account votes with the voting power it held when voting opened. If enough XRD takes part and the threshold is met, it passes.

detail_hints.system: Governance system running this vote: who organises it, publishes the tally and carries out the result. The link opens its official website.
detail_hints.kind_proposal: Formal proposal: the vote that decides a specific change. It usually follows a temperature check that gathered enough support.
detail_hints.kind_temperature_check: Temperature check: a non-binding vote to gauge community support for an idea before it becomes a formal proposal.
detail_hints.kind_election: Election: a Majority Judgment election where voters grade every candidate to fill council seats.
detail_hints.number: This vote's number within its system. Proposals and temperature checks are numbered separately.
detail_hints.parameters: Set of rules the vote was created with. It sets the quorum, the approval threshold and the duration that apply to it.
detail_hints.quorum: Minimum voting power, in XRD, that must take part for the result to be valid. If it is not reached, the vote does not count, whichever option wins.
detail_hints.threshold: Share of the votes in favour, out of votes in favour and against, needed to pass. Abstentions do not count.
detail_hints.max_options: How many options each voter may pick on their ballot.
detail_hints.duration: How long the vote stays open, from opening to closing.
detail_hints.starts: Opening date and time. Each account's voting power is taken from its balances at this moment, so buying XRD afterwards adds no votes.
detail_hints.ends: Closing date and time. From then on no votes are accepted and the result is final.
detail_hints.voters: Distinct addresses that have voted. If one changed its mind, only its latest vote counts.

historical.heading: Historical voting methods comparison
historical.intro: Sums every ballot, address, and millions of XRD across all governance proposals and temperature checks, comparing how each voting method would have performed overall: how many outcomes would have changed, cumulative ballots and eligible XRD, and average decentralisation.
historical.kpi_effective_hint: {resistance} resistance · {pct} decentralisation · quorum in {valid} of {total} votes
historical.tip_kpi_effective: Method with the best combination of all three factors: manipulation resistance, average decentralisation, and share of votes reaching quorum (geometric mean of the three).
historical.tip_kpi_ineffective: Method with the worst combination of manipulation resistance, average decentralisation, and share of votes reaching quorum.
historical.kpi_most_changes_hint: would have produced a different outcome (another winner, rejection, or no quorum) in {n} of {total} votes vs 1 XRD = 1 vote
historical.tip_kpi_most_changes: Method whose verdict (approved, rejected, no quorum, different winning option, or no qualifying voters) differs in the most votes compared with the current method (1 XRD = 1 vote).
historical.kpi_current_hint: control >50 % on average (out of {voters} voters · {pct} decentralisation · {avg} XRD/vote)
historical.tip_col_changes: How many historical votes would have produced a different outcome from 1 XRD = 1 vote under this method.
historical.tip_col_ballots: Total individual ballots cast across all votes that count under this method.
historical.tip_col_xrd: Sum of the XRD held by qualifying addresses across all analysed votes.
historical.tip_changes: This method would have changed the outcome in {n} of {total} votes ({pct}) compared with the current method (1 XRD = 1 vote).
historical.tip_changes_zero: This method would have given the same outcome as 1 XRD = 1 vote in all {total} votes.
historical.tip_ballots: Out of {total} cumulative ballots in history, {n} count under this method ({out} are excluded for not meeting its requirements).
historical.tip_ballots_share: {pct} of the {total} cumulative ballots ({n} of {total}) count under this method.
historical.tip_xrd: {total} cumulative XRD across {votes} evaluated votes (average of {avg} XRD per vote).
historical.tip_spread: Average of {n} addresses to control 50 % of the weight across {votes} votes · {eff} effective voters on average · {spread} decentralisation ({level}).
historical.detail_decisive: Across the {votes} votes that reached quorum and had a valid result under this method, on average just {count} addresses ({pct} of the {of} voting per vote, holding {xrd} XRD per vote and {totalXrd} XRD cumulative) were enough to decide the outcome, even if everyone else had voted the other way.
historical.tip_detail_votes: Number of historical votes where at least one address met this method's requirements ({votes} of {total}).
historical.tip_detail_effective: Arithmetic mean of effective voters across the {votes} evaluated votes. In each vote it is computed as 1 / Σ(weightᵢ / total weight)²: the number of equal-weight voters that would produce the same concentration.
historical.tip_detail_xrd: Sum of the XRD held by qualifying addresses in each of the {votes} evaluated votes ({total} XRD total; average of {avg} XRD per vote). If an address voted in multiple proposals, its XRD is summed in each vote it joined.
historical.tip_detail_spread: Arithmetic mean of the decentralisation score across the {votes} evaluated votes ({pct}). In each vote it is computed as effective voters / voting addresses (Simpson evenness, from 0 % to 100 %; 100 % when every address weighs the same).
historical.changed_list_title: Votes whose outcome would have changed ({n})
historical.guide_open: See how this method is aggregated across history
historical.guide_intro: This method is simulated independently on every vote in the selected history, preserving each vote's own rules, and then aggregated into overall reliability metrics.
historical.guide_step1: Vote-by-vote simulation: applies this rule to each of the {totalVotes} historical votes using the balances and account ages at the moment each vote opened ({evaluated} votes had qualifying voters; {ballots} cumulative ballots counted).
historical.guide_step2: Outcome flips: compares each vote's verdict under this method against 1 XRD = 1 vote. Here {changed} of {decided} votes would have produced a different outcome.
historical.guide_step2_reference: Reference baseline: this is the current rule (1 XRD = 1 vote) against which every other method's outcome flips are compared across the {totalVotes} votes.
historical.guide_step3: Average decentralisation & quorum: averages the Nakamoto coefficient ({nakamoto} addresses) and Simpson evenness ({spread}) across evaluated votes, and counts how many of the {totalVotes} analysed votes still meet quorum ({valid} of {totalVotes}).
historical.guide_step4: Balance & effectiveness scores: Balance is the geometric mean of manipulation resistance and average decentralisation; Effectiveness adds the share of votes reaching quorum so rules that exclude too much XRD are penalised.

compare.heading: What would another voting method have decided?
compare.intro: Votes are weighed today at 1 XRD = 1 vote: an account with 1,000 XRD has 1,000 votes. Here the same ballots are counted with other rules. Every voter keeps their choice and their XRD; only how much the vote weighs changes. It shows whether the result depends on the method and how centralised or decentralised power is under each one.
compare.intro_election: In a Majority Judgment election every voter must grade all candidates, so raw vote counts per candidate are identical. Here we re-run the exact 60 % quantile and Majority Gauge algorithm under each weighting rule to see whether the elected council changes and how concentrated voting power is.
compare.election_overlap_tip: {matched} of {total} elected seats match 1 XRD = 1 vote ({pct}).
compare.election_current_guide_open: See how the current voting method is calculated
compare.election_current_conclusions_council_tit: Elected council ({seats} seats) & agreement with other methods
compare.election_current_conclusions_quorum_text: The current method gathers {eligible} XRD against a quorum of {quorum} XRD ({pct}).
compare.election_current_conclusions_decisive_te: Under 1 XRD = 1 vote, {count} of the {total} addresses ({pct}, holding {xrd} XRD) reach that {quantilePct}: if they agree on a grade, they alone set any candidate's qualifying grade regardless of how everyone else votes.
compare.election_current_resistance_intro_1: 1 XRD = 1 vote has high Sybil resistance: splitting one wallet into 1,000 wallets creates zero extra votes because weight depends strictly on total XRD at the snapshot.
compare.election_current_resistance_intro_2: In return, it places no cap on capital concentration and requires no prior holding time: any single wallet or group holding {quantilePct} of participating XRD at the snapshot controls 100 % of the qualifying grade.
compare.election_current_resistance_table_note: Real impact of each technique on 1 XRD = 1 vote (100 % immune to wallet splitting, 100 % dependent on snapshot capital).
compare.election_current_resistance_cheap_sybil_: Nothing meaningful: 1,000 wallets of 1 XRD only contribute 1,000 real XRD, with no multiplier.
Strict linearity (1 XRD = 1 vote): splitting capital creates zero extra voting power.
compare.election_current_resistance_funded_sybil: Only its real XRD share (without a capital majority it cannot control the {quantilePct} qualifying grade).
Without a majority of snapshot XRD, spreading capital across hundreds of wallets gives no advantage.
compare.election_current_resistance_opportunisti: 100 % of any candidate's qualifying grade if it holds > {quantilePct} of participating XRD at the snapshot.
Nothing in the rule: no wallet cap, no account age gate, and no TWAB requirement.
compare.election_current_resistance_split_whale_: 100 % (identical to using 1 single wallet; splitting neither helps nor hurts).
Nothing in the rule: only the need to hold the capital at the snapshot block.
compare.election_current_resistance_veteran_whal: 100 % of the qualifying grade if it holds > {quantilePct} of participating XRD.
Nothing in the rule: account age adds or subtracts no weight.
compare.election_current_resistance_veteran_sybi: Only its real XRD share (no multiplier from wallet count or account age).
Strict XRD linearity: holding veteran accounts without a capital majority cannot sway the outcome.
compare.election_current_resistance_nation_state: 100 % of the outcome if it gathers > {quantilePct} of participating XRD.
Only the financial cost of acquiring or controlling > {quantilePct} of participating XRD.
compare.election_current_resistance_nuance_sybil: Immune to Sybil (0 % gain from splitting wallets): creating thousands of new or veteran low-balance wallets cannot manipulate the outcome.
compare.election_current_resistance_nuance_whale: Vulnerable to capital concentration and last-minute buys: in this vote, {count} of {total} addresses ({pct}) hold {quantilePct} of the weight and can unilaterally fix any candidate's grade.
compare.election_current_resistance_summary: In short: 1 XRD = 1 vote is the simplest rule and completely immune to wallet splitting, but concentrates decisive power in the largest whales and requires no prior holding time.
compare.election_consensus_hint: All 4 families carry equal weight (25 % each); within each family, more Sybil-resistant and decentralised rules weigh up to 4× more.
compare.election_consensus_card_tip: {name} · Consensus #{rank} ({pct} weighted · elected in {elected}/{total} methods) · Avg rank #{avgRank} · Most frequent qualifying grade across {total} methods: {grade} · Current (1 XRD = 1 vote): {current}
compare.election_consensus_guide_open: See how the weighted ranking is calculated
compare.election_consensus_guide_intro: Instead of a raw count (where a family with more variants or Sybil-vulnerable rules would dominate), this ranking combines all {n} evaluated methods (including 1 XRD = 1 vote) in a balanced, transparent way.
compare.election_consensus_guide_step1: Equal weight across all 4 families (25 % each): Wealth, Address, Seniority, and Hybrid each carry the exact same total weight so no philosophy dominates simply by having more variants in the list.
compare.election_consensus_guide_step2: Quality weighting within each family: each method gets weight 0.25 + 0.75 × effectiveness (normalized within its family), where effectiveness combines Sybil resistance, decentralisation, and quorum. All {n} methods participate, while stronger rules weigh up to 4× more.
compare.election_consensus_guide_step3: Consensus score: each candidate sums the weights of the methods where they are elected (plus half the weight when tied at the seat cutoff). Each card also shows the raw N/{n} count.
compare.election_consensus_guide_step4: Tie-breaking and full ordering: ties in weighted share are broken by lower weighted average rank (Ø #N) across all {n} methods, and finally by the candidate's most frequent qualifying grade.
compare.election_consensus_guide_step5: Most frequent qualifying grade & eligible voters: under each method, a candidate earns a single qualifying grade (the grade where cumulative weight from Excellent downward reaches the cutoff quantile, e.g. 60 %). The grade shown on each card is the one accumulating the most weight across all {n} methods — not the raw ballot count from the Results tab. All methods only count addresses with > 0 XRD at the snapshot (with each rule applying its own balance, age, or staking filters).
compare.election_resistance_intro_1: Compared with 1 XRD = 1 vote (where a single whale controlling 60 % of XRD at the snapshot dominates 100 % of the outcome), the weighted ranking across all {n} methods is far harder to capture alone because it splits weight across 4 fixed 25 % families (Wealth, Address, Seniority, and Hybrid) and weights stronger, more decentralised rules up to 4× higher.
compare.election_resistance_intro_2: This forces an attacker to combine mutually conflicting vectors: large capital + splitting across hundreds of wallets + holding time (90-day TWAB / staking) + 1 to 2 years of account age.
compare.election_resistance_table_title: Maximum controllable weight by attack technique
compare.election_resistance_table_note: Exact share computed from the live normalized weights of the {n} evaluated methods in this vote (4 families × 25 %).
compare.election_resistance_metric_share_tip: Maximum controllable weight ({pct}): highest share of voting weight this technique can capture under this rule (0 % = fully blocked; 100 % = full control of the outcome).
compare.election_resistance_metric_difficulty_ti: Difficulty score ({score}/10): 0/10 = trivial attack with no capital or wait and full capture; 10/10 = fully blocked by the rule (0 % weight). Combines the technique's operational cost (base {base}/10: capital {capital}/6, time/lockup {time}/2, coordination {coord}/1) with this rule's containment (max weight {pct}).
compare.election_resistance_legend_share_desc: maximum share of voting power this technique can capture under this rule (0 % = fully blocked; 100 % = full control of the outcome).
compare.election_resistance_legend_difficulty_de: score of how hard it is to execute the attack successfully, combining its operational cost (capital, time/lockup, and coordination) with this rule's containment (0/10 = trivial with full capture; 10/10 = blocked by the rule).
compare.election_resistance_legend_global_desc: overall resistance rating of the rule, computed as 50 % × structural anti-Sybil resistance (Very low 0/10, Low 3.3/10, Medium 6.7/10, High 10/10) + 50 % × 7-attack defense (70 % × weakest-link minimum difficulty + 30 % × mean difficulty across the 7 vectors).
compare.election_resistance_global_score_tip: Overall score ({score}/10): 50 % structural anti-Sybil ({sybil}/10) + 50 % 7-attack defense ({attacks}/10 = 70 % weakest link {min}/10 + 30 % mean {avg}/10). Average controllable weight: {avgShare}.
compare.election_resistance_legend_decent_desc: effective distribution of voting power across participants measured from spread (1 − normalised HHI × 10: 0/10 = full concentration; 10/10 = uniform distribution).
compare.election_resistance_legend_final_desc: geometric mean √(Resistance × Decentralisation) out of 10; requires strength in both dimensions and penalises either one dropping near zero.
compare.election_resistance_decent_score_tip: Decentralisation score ({score}/10): matches {spreadPct} spread (1 − normalised HHI).

compare.election_resistance_ranking_cell_nakamot: Nakamoto coefficient: {n} wallets needed to exceed 50 % of voting power
compare.election_resistance_ranking_cell_top1_ti: The single largest wallet holds {pct} of total voting weight
compare.election_resistance_ranking_cell_resista: Overall resistance score: {score}/10 ({level} tier · weakest link {min}/10)
compare.election_resistance_ranking_cell_na_tip: Not enough data in this vote
compare.election_resistance_ranking_expand_all_t: Expand candidate cards for all methods
compare.election_card_tied_tip: Exact tie at the seat cutoff (identical grade, band, and p/q shares); Majority Judgment does not break ties by ID.
compare.election_card_below_min_tip: Falls below the minimum required grade ({minGrade}) under this method.
compare.election_card_dropped_tip: Drops outside the {seats} seats compared with 1 XRD = 1 vote.
compare.election_card_entered_tip: Enters the {seats} elected seats compared with 1 XRD = 1 vote.
compare.election_resistance_attack_cheap_sybil_t: Cheap last-minute Sybil (thousands of new 1 XRD wallets)
compare.election_resistance_attack_cheap_sybil_c: The 7 very-low-resistance rules without age or balance floors (quadratic, cube root, logarithmic, tiered, 1 address = 1 vote, address + age, quadratic + seniority), the address half of 50/50 hybrid, and the headcount chamber of double majority.
compare.election_resistance_attack_cheap_sybil_b: Seniority rules (25 %), all 8 ≥ 1-year anti-Sybil Address rules, almost all of Wealth, and most Hybrid rules.
compare.election_resistance_attack_funded_sybil_: Funded last-minute Sybil (hundreds of new wallets with ≥ 10,000 XRD, without capital majority)
Everything above plus 1 address with minimum balance (≥ 10,000 XRD) and the 10,000 XRD wallet cap.
Capital/time-gated Seniority rules (25 %), all 8 ≥ 1-year Address rules, all veteran/TWAB Hybrid rules, and linear or higher-cap rules.
compare.election_resistance_attack_opportunistic: Opportunistic whale (1 new wallet with > 60 % of XRD right before snapshot)

Linear rules with no age gate (1 XRD = 1 vote, deductible, staked-only if staked, whales-only), partial share on 90-day TWAB (and caps), seniority bonus weighted by capital, the capital half of 50/50 hybrid, and double majority's capital chamber.
Wallet caps (fixed or percentage), no-top-1, no-whales, all of Address (25 %), almost all of Seniority, and almost all Hybrid rules.
compare.election_resistance_attack_split_whale_t: Split whale at last minute (> 60 % of XRD spread across hundreds of new wallets right before snapshot)
compare.election_resistance_attack_split_whale_c: All of Wealth (25 %), the 3 non-aged Address rules, seniority bonus, the recent quarter of 90-day TWAB, and Hybrid rules without veteran or continuous-holding gates.
compare.election_resistance_attack_split_whale_b: Almost all of Seniority (≥ 1–2 year veterans and 90-day minimum), all 8 ≥ 1-year Address rules, and all veteran or time-locked Hybrid rules.
compare.election_resistance_attack_veteran_whale: Veteran whale (1 single > 2-year wallet with > 60 % of XRD staked & 90-day TWAB)
Linear Wealth rules, 6 of 7 Seniority rules (all except veteran headcount), whales-only, marginal veterans, and the capital half of 50/50 hybrids and capital chambers.
All hard/percentage cap rules, no-top-1, no-whales, and all of Address (25 %).
compare.election_resistance_attack_veteran_sybil: Prepared veteran Sybil farm (hundreds of > 2-year wallets with split non-majority capital)

The 4 very-low Wealth rules, quadratic + seniority bonus, 4 of 11 Address rules (blocked by ≥ 10k/100k/1M XRD floors), veteran headcount, anti-Sybil quadratic, the address half of 50/50 hybrid, and the double-majority chamber.
All linear and high-cap Wealth, Seniority, and Hybrid rules, veteran hybrid (requires ≥ 10k XRD), and the 10k–1M XRD Address floors.
compare.election_resistance_attack_nation_state_: Full pre-planned attack (hundreds of > 2-year wallets + > 60 % of XRD split + staking + 90-day TWAB)
Bypasses all caps, meets 1–2 year age, all minimum balances (1k–1M XRD), 90-day TWAB, staking, and address count.
Nothing purely on-chain; requires locking massive real capital for 90 days–2 years and planning 2 years in advance.
compare.election_resistance_nuance_impose: Imposing an unpopular candidate from 0 % into the council (> 50–60 %): no single technique exceeds half of weighted consensus (the highest single vector caps at {maxSingle}). Only the full pre-planned attack works.
compare.election_resistance_nuance_impose_high: The largest single attack vector captures up to {maxSingle} of the weighted consensus in this vote.
compare.election_resistance_nuance_tie: Tipping a razor-thin cutoff (e.g. 42 % vs. 48 %): a cheap last-minute Sybil attack can capture up to {cheapSybil} of weighted consensus — enough to nudge a close tie, though never enough to overturn a clear majority.
compare.election_resistance_summary: In short: as a decision rule it delivers solid resistance against whales and last-minute buys; if adopted as a binding rule, lowering weights on very-low-resistance rules and tightening split exposure would sharply reduce even that {cheapSybil} margin on razor-thin ties.
compare.method_conc_nobody_detail: None of the {excluded} valid snapshot voters met this rule's requirements.

compare.election_guide_intro: Because every voter must grade all candidates, changing the voting method does not change how many ballots each candidate gets — it changes how much each voter's grades weigh when building each candidate's grade distribution.
compare.election_guide_double_majority: Double majority rule: in addition to weighting by XRD, each candidate must also reach at least {minGrade} when counting 1 address = 1 vote on the qualifying pool.
compare.election_guide_step1: Voter weights: this rule assigns each qualifying account its weight. Here {counted} of {total} accounts count ({eff} effective voters; {nakamoto} addresses control 50 % of the weight).
compare.election_guide_step2: {quantilePct} grade quantile ({quantile}): for each candidate, the weights of the {counted} counted accounts are accumulated from Excellent down to Poor. The qualifying grade is the highest grade where the cumulative weight reaches at least {quantilePct}.
compare.election_guide_step3: Majority Gauge tie-break (Bands A, B, C): candidates with the same qualifying grade are ordered by p (weight strictly above that grade) vs q (weight strictly below). Band A (p > q) ranks ahead of Band B (p = q) and Band C (p < q).
compare.election_guide_step4: Grade floor & seat cutoff: only candidates with a qualifying grade of {minGrade} or higher can win one of the {seats} seats. Exact ties at the seat cutoff are preserved as Tied instead of being broken arbitrarily.
compare.standard_guide_open: See how this method is calculated in this vote
compare.standard_guide_intro: Every voter keeps their chosen option and their XRD; only the weight assigned to each address changes before tallying the ballot.
compare.standard_guide_double_majority: Double majority rule: to pass, support must reach at least {threshold} both when weighted by XRD and when counting 1 address = 1 vote.
compare.standard_guide_step1: Voter weights: this rule assigns each qualifying account its weight. Here {counted} of {total} accounts count ({eff} effective voters; {nakamoto} addresses control 50 % of the weight).
compare.standard_guide_step2: Weighted tally per option: each counted voter's weight is added to the option(s) they selected. In For/Against votes, approval share is computed over decisive votes (abstentions do not count against approval).
compare.standard_guide_step3: Quorum in real XRD: quorum is always checked against the real XRD held by the accounts that count under this rule ({xrd} XRD counted vs {quorum} XRD minimum), not the transformed weight.
compare.standard_guide_step3_no_quorum: Eligible XRD: this vote has no minimum XRD quorum; {xrd} XRD come from the accounts that count under this rule.
compare.standard_guide_step4: Final verdict: a For/Against vote passes if quorum is met and approval reaches at least {threshold}. In multi-option ballots, the option with the highest total weight leads.
compare.standard_guide_step4_no_threshold: Final verdict: this ballot has no binary approval threshold, so the option with the highest total weight leads (subject to quorum if required).

compare.g_nakamoto: Two measures of how spread power is. "Control 50 %" is the Nakamoto coefficient: the fewest addresses that together hold more than half of the weight. The degree of decentralisation is effective voters over voters (Simpson evenness, from the Herfindahl index): 100 % when all weigh the same. It takes every address into account and compares votes with few and many voters.

compare.g_effective: How many voters there would be if they all weighed the same and power were just as centralised. If 150 accounts vote but amount to 10 effective voters, a few decide.

linear.name: 1 XRD = 1 vote
linear.rule: Every XRD is a vote: 1,000 XRD weigh 1,000 votes. This is the method votes use today.
linear.attack: Splitting into addresses adds no votes. The only way to weigh more is to get more XRD, buying or borrowing it before the vote opens.

deductible_linear.name: 1 XRD = 1 vote with {min} XRD deductible
deductible_linear.rule: Only the balance above {min} XRD counts (the first {min} XRD of each account are deducted). Strictly superadditive: splitting capital across accounts loses votes instead of gaining them.
deductible_linear.attack: Splitting across accounts actively penalises the attacker ({min} XRD lost per extra address). The only way to weigh more is to concentrate more real capital.

staked_only.name: Staked XRD only
staked_only.rule: 1 XRD = 1 vote, but only XRD delegated to validators when the vote opened counts. Excludes liquid balances held in wallets or exchanges.
staked_only.attack: Splitting adds no extra votes, and last-minute bought or borrowed liquid XRD does not count unless staked in validators.

capped_10k.name: Capped at 10,000 XRD per address
capped_10k.rule: Like today, but no address can weigh more than 10,000 XRD: a very low cap that evens wallets out a lot.
capped_10k.attack: The cap is dodged by splitting the XRD into addresses of 10,000 XRD or less; in practice it is back to 1 XRD = 1 vote and it takes capital.

capped_100k.name: Capped at 100,000 XRD per address
capped_100k.rule: Like today, but no address can weigh more than 100,000 XRD.
capped_100k.attack: The cap is dodged by splitting the XRD into addresses of 100,000 XRD or less; in practice it is back to 1 XRD = 1 vote and it takes capital.

capped.name: Capped at 1,000,000 XRD per address
capped.rule: Like today, but no address can weigh more than {cap} XRD. It limits the largest wallets without taking their vote away.
capped.attack: The cap is dodged by splitting the XRD into addresses under {cap} XRD, so in practice it is back to 1 XRD = 1 vote: it takes capital.

capped_5m.name: Capped at 5,000,000 XRD per address
capped_5m.rule: Like today, but no address can weigh more than 5 million XRD: it limits large whales without affecting mid-sized wallets.
capped_5m.attack: The cap is dodged by splitting the XRD into addresses of 5 million or less; in practice it is back to 1 XRD = 1 vote and it takes capital.

capped_10m.name: Capped at 10,000,000 XRD per address
capped_10m.rule: Like today, but no address can weigh more than 10 million XRD: it only limits the largest whales.
capped_10m.attack: The cap is dodged by splitting the XRD into addresses of 10 million or less; in practice it is back to 1 XRD = 1 vote and it takes capital.

capped_share.name: Capped at {share} of the total
capped_share.rule: 1 XRD = 1 vote, but no address can weigh more than {share} of all the XRD that voted. The cap grows with turnout.
capped_share.attack: Like the fixed cap: split across addresses, each part stays under {share} and counts in full.

capped_share_5.name: Capped at 5 % of the total
capped_share_5.rule: 1 XRD = 1 vote, but no address can weigh more than 5 % of all the XRD that voted.
capped_share_5.attack: Split across addresses, each part stays under 5 % and counts in full: it takes capital.

capped_share_10.name: Capped at 10 % of the total
capped_share_10.rule: 1 XRD = 1 vote, but no address can weigh more than 10 % of all the XRD that voted.
capped_share_10.attack: Split across addresses, each part stays under 10 % and counts in full: it takes capital.

quadratic.name: Quadratic voting
quadratic.rule: The vote weighs the square root of the balance: 100 XRD give 10 votes and 1,000,000 XRD give 1,000. Holding more still counts, but each extra XRD counts less.
quadratic.attack: Splitting multiplies the vote: 1,000,000 XRD in one address are worth 1,000 votes, but split into 1,000,000 addresses of 1 XRD they are worth 1,000,000.

cube_root.name: Cube root
cube_root.rule: The vote weighs the cube root of the balance: 1,000 XRD give 10 votes and 1,000,000 XRD give 100. It sits between quadratic and logarithmic voting.
cube_root.attack: Even more sensitive to splitting than quadratic: the smaller the parts, the more votes.

logarithmic.name: Logarithmic voting
logarithmic.rule: One vote is added each time the balance grows tenfold: 1,000 XRD give about 3 votes and 1,000,000 XRD about 6. The balance barely matters.
logarithmic.attack: An address with 1 XRD weighs almost as much as one with millions, so many small addresses multiply the vote.

tiered.name: Balance tiers
tiered.rule: 1 to 5 votes by balance: under 1,000 XRD, 1 vote; from 1,000, 2; from 10,000, 3; from 100,000, 4; from 1,000,000, 5.
tiered.attack: Any address with a balance has at least 1 vote: 1,000 addresses with 1 XRD outweigh one with 100 million.

one_address.name: 1 address = 1 vote
one_address.rule: Every address weighs the same, whatever it holds.
one_address.attack: New addresses are free and there is no KYC: one person can vote with as many addresses as they like, each holding just enough for the fee.

one_address_min.name: 1 address = 1 vote, from {min} XRD
one_address_min.rule: Only addresses holding at least {min} XRD count, and they all weigh the same.
one_address_min.attack: Each extra vote costs {min} XRD in a new address. Whoever has a lot of capital splits it across many addresses and gains a huge number of votes.

one_address_sybil.name: 1 address = 1 vote, sybil-resistant (≥ {balance} XRD)
one_address_sybil.rule: All weigh the same, but only addresses with at least {balance} XRD and {years_sybil} year of age count. Creating many new accounts does not help.
one_address_sybil.attack: New accounts do not count: it takes addresses set up over {years_sybil} year ago holding {balance} XRD each. Possible, but it has to be planned well ahead.

one_address_sybil_10k.name: 1 address = 1 vote, sybil-resistant (≥ 10,000 XRD)
one_address_sybil_10k.rule: All weigh the same, but only addresses with at least 10,000 XRD and {years_sybil} year of age count.
one_address_sybil_10k.attack: Requires addresses over {years_sybil} year old holding 10,000 XRD each. Multiplying votes requires meaningful capital prepared ahead of time.

one_address_sybil_100k.name: 1 address = 1 vote, sybil-resistant (≥ 100,000 XRD)
one_address_sybil_100k.rule: All weigh the same, but only addresses with at least 100,000 XRD and {years_sybil} year of age count.
one_address_sybil_100k.attack: Requires addresses over {years_sybil} year old holding 100,000 XRD each. Stops cheap mass attacks, though a whale could still split across old accounts.

one_address_sybil_1m.name: 1 address = 1 vote, sybil-resistant (≥ 1,000,000 XRD)
one_address_sybil_1m.rule: All weigh the same, but only addresses with at least 1,000,000 XRD and {years_sybil} year of age count.
one_address_sybil_1m.attack: Each vote requires an account over {years_sybil} year old holding 1,000,000 XRD. Very expensive to game, though it excludes almost all smaller holders.

one_address_sybil_age.name: 1 address = 1 vote, sybil-resistant (≥ {balance} XRD), +1 vote/yr
one_address_sybil_age.rule: Only addresses with at least {balance} XRD and {years_sybil} year of age count. Each has 1 vote, plus 1 vote for each full year of age.
one_address_sybil_age.attack: New accounts do not count: it takes addresses set up over {years_sybil} year ago holding {balance} XRD, and the older they are, the more votes each one gives. Possible, but it has to be planned years ahead.

one_address_sybil_age_10k.name: 1 address = 1 vote, sybil-resistant (≥ 10,000 XRD), +1 vote/yr
one_address_sybil_age_10k.rule: Only addresses with at least 10,000 XRD and {years_sybil} year of age count. Each has 1 vote, plus 1 vote for each full year of age.
one_address_sybil_age_10k.attack: Requires accounts over {years_sybil} year old holding 10,000 XRD each; older accounts carry more votes.

one_address_sybil_age_100k.name: 1 address = 1 vote, sybil-resistant (≥ 100,000 XRD), +1 vote/yr
one_address_sybil_age_100k.rule: Only addresses with at least 100,000 XRD and {years_sybil} year of age count. Each has 1 vote, plus 1 vote for each full year of age.
one_address_sybil_age_100k.attack: Requires accounts over {years_sybil} year old holding 100,000 XRD each, combining a higher capital barrier with account age.

one_address_sybil_age_1m.name: 1 address = 1 vote, sybil-resistant (≥ 1,000,000 XRD), +1 vote/yr
one_address_sybil_age_1m.rule: Only addresses with at least 1,000,000 XRD and {years_sybil} year of age count. Each has 1 vote, plus 1 vote for each full year of age.
one_address_sybil_age_1m.attack: Requires accounts over {years_sybil} year old holding 1,000,000 XRD each; very costly to attack but highly restrictive for smaller voters.

address_age.name: 1 address = 1 vote, plus 1 per year
address_age.rule: Each address has 1 vote, plus 1 extra vote for each full year of age. The balance does not matter; loyalty does.
address_age.attack: New addresses already have 1 vote, so creating many works just as with 1 address = 1 vote.

one_year.name: Accounts 1 year or older
one_year.rule: 1 XRD = 1 vote, but only accounts that were 1 year old or more when the vote opened count.
one_year.attack: Age belongs to the account, not to the XRD: freshly bought XRD can go into an account over a year old. Splitting gains nothing; it takes capital.

veterans.name: Veterans only ({years}+ years)
veterans.rule: 1 XRD = 1 vote, but only accounts that were {years} years old or more when the vote opened count.
veterans.attack: An account {years} or more years old is enough to hold XRD bought at the last minute. It leaves out newcomers, not buyers.

veterans_address.name: Veterans, 1 address = 1 vote
veterans_address.rule: Only accounts {years} years old or more count, and they all weigh the same.
veterans_address.attack: It takes many addresses created {years} or more years ago, even with a tiny balance. It cannot be improvised, but it is cheap for whoever prepared it.

veterans_bonus.name: Veterans with an age bonus
veterans_bonus.rule: Only accounts {years} years old or more count, and every full year adds {bonus} to the vote: 2 years weigh ×1.5 and 3 years ×1.75.
veterans_bonus.attack: Splitting gains nothing and the bonus belongs to the account, not to the XRD: in an old account, freshly bought XRD get the bonus too.

seniority_bonus.name: Age bonus for everyone
seniority_bonus.rule: Every account counts: 1 XRD = 1 vote, plus {bonus} for each full year of age.
seniority_bonus.attack: Splitting gains nothing; new accounts just get no bonus. It takes capital.

twab_90d.name: 90-day time-weighted average (TWAB)
twab_90d.rule: Weighs the average XRD (liquid and staked) held across the 90 days before the vote opened (sampled every 30 days). Neutralises last-minute buying or borrowing.
twab_90d.attack: Splitting adds no extra votes and buying XRD right before opening only gives a quarter of the weight: it takes real capital held for months.

held_90d.name: 90-day continuous minimum balance
held_90d.rule: Only the minimum XRD balance (liquid and staked) continuously held across all 90-day checkpoints before opening counts.
held_90d.attack: Splitting gains nothing and any XRD bought or borrowed in the last 90 days weighs zero: capital must be committed 3 months ahead.

hybrid_half.name: Mixed 50 / 50
hybrid_half.rule: Half of the weight is shared by XRD and the other half equally between addresses.
hybrid_half.attack: Half of the weight is shared per address: with thousands of empty addresses, one person takes almost all of that half.

hybrid_half_veterans.name: Hardened 50 / 50 (veterans from {min} XRD)
hybrid_half_veterans.rule: Only accounts at least {years} years old holding {min} XRD or more count. Half of the weight is proportional to their XRD and the other half is shared equally between those accounts.
hybrid_half_veterans.attack: New or lightly funded accounts do not count. Gaming the equal half requires preparing many accounts {years} or more years ahead with {min} XRD each.

double_majority.name: Double majority
double_majority.rule: To pass it must clear the threshold twice: counting 1 XRD = 1 vote and counting 1 address = 1 vote. Like the European Union's qualified majority.
double_majority.attack: Passing takes capital and winning by addresses too, but blocking only takes empty addresses voting against.

double_majority_sybil.name: Hardened double majority (capital + veteran community)
double_majority_sybil.rule: To pass it must clear the threshold in two chambers: by capital (1 XRD = 1 vote) and by community (1 address = 1 vote, only accounts at least {years} years old holding {min} XRD or more).
double_majority_sybil.attack: A whale cannot pass a vote alone without veteran community support, and blocking is no longer free: it requires controlling many accounts {years} or more years old with {min} XRD each.

capped_veterans.name: Capped at {cap} XRD, veterans only ({years}+ years)
capped_veterans.rule: 1 XRD = 1 vote capped at {cap} XRD per address, and only accounts {years} or more years old count. Limits whales while blocking last-minute splitting into new accounts.
capped_veterans.attack: Splitting never multiplies votes beyond 1 XRD = 1 vote, and dodging the cap requires both real capital and multiple separate accounts prepared {years} or more years ahead.

capped_veterans_5m.name: Capped at 5,000,000 XRD, veterans only ({years}+ years)
capped_veterans_5m.rule: 1 XRD = 1 vote capped at 5 million XRD per address, and only accounts {years} or more years old count. Limits large whales while blocking last-minute splitting into new accounts.
capped_veterans_5m.attack: Splitting never multiplies votes beyond 1 XRD = 1 vote, and dodging the 5 million cap requires real capital and multiple accounts prepared {years} or more years ahead.

capped_veterans_10m.name: Capped at 10,000,000 XRD, veterans only ({years}+ years)
capped_veterans_10m.rule: 1 XRD = 1 vote capped at 10 million XRD per address, and only accounts {years} or more years old count. Only reins in the largest whales while blocking splitting into new accounts.
capped_veterans_10m.attack: Splitting never multiplies votes beyond 1 XRD = 1 vote, and dodging the 10 million cap requires real capital and multiple accounts prepared {years} or more years ahead.

capped_share_veterans_1.name: Capped at {share} of total, veterans only ({years}+ years)
capped_share_veterans_1.rule: 1 XRD = 1 vote, but no address can weigh more than {share} of participating veteran XRD, and only accounts {years} or more years old count. Maximum decentralisation within high security.
capped_share_veterans_1.attack: Splitting never yields more than 1 vote per XRD, and dodging the {share} cap requires real capital spread across dozens of accounts prepared {years} or more years ahead.

capped_share_veterans.name: Capped at {share_veterans} of total, veterans only ({years}+ years)
capped_share_veterans.rule: 1 XRD = 1 vote, but no address can weigh more than {share_veterans} of participating veteran XRD, and only accounts {years} or more years old count. Scales with turnout and guarantees decentralisation.
capped_share_veterans.attack: Splitting never yields more than 1 vote per XRD, and dodging the {share_veterans} cap requires real capital spread across accounts prepared {years} or more years ahead.

staked_capped_share.name: Staked XRD only, {share_veterans} cap
staked_capped_share.rule: Only XRD delegated to validators when the vote opened counts, and no address can weigh more than {share_veterans} of participating staked XRD.
staked_capped_share.attack: Splitting never exceeds 1 vote per XRD and requires keeping capital genuinely staked in validators, spread across accounts to dodge the {share_veterans} cap.

twab_90d_capped_share.name: 90-day average (TWAB), {share_veterans} cap
twab_90d_capped_share.rule: Weighs the 90-day time-weighted average balance (liquid + staked) held before the vote opened, capped at {share_veterans} of total participating TWAB per address.
twab_90d_capped_share.attack: Blocks last-minute buys or loans (requires holding XRD for months), limits top whales via the {share_veterans} cap, and splitting never exceeds 1 XRD = 1 vote.

marginal_veterans.name: Diminishing marginal brackets, veterans only ({years}+ years)
marginal_veterans.rule: Only accounts {years} or more years old count. The first {bracket_first} XRD weigh 100 %, {bracket_first} to {bracket_second} XRD weigh 50 %, and anything above {bracket_second} XRD weighs 10 %. Reduces concentration without silencing large long-term holders.
marginal_veterans.attack: Splitting never exceeds 1 XRD = 1 vote; avoiding the marginal reduction requires real capital split across {bracket_first} XRD accounts prepared {years} or more years ahead.

quadratic_seniority.name: Quadratic with an age bonus
quadratic_seniority.rule: Square root of the balance, plus {bonus} for each full year of account age.
quadratic_seniority.attack: New addresses count (with no bonus), so splitting into many small addresses multiplies the vote as with quadratic voting.

sybil_quadratic.name: Sybil-resistant quadratic
sybil_quadratic.rule: Square root of the balance, but only addresses with at least {balance} XRD and {years_sybil} year of age count.
sybil_quadratic.attack: Splitting multiplies the vote, but each address needs {balance} XRD and {years_sybil} year of age: the accounts have to be prepared ahead.

no_top1.name: Without the largest address
no_top1.rule: 1 XRD = 1 vote, leaving out the address with the most XRD. It shows whether a single wallet decides the result.
no_top1.attack: The exclusion is dodged by splitting the XRD into two addresses so neither is the largest. In the end it takes capital, as with 1 XRD = 1 vote.

no_whales.name: Without the {n} largest
no_whales.rule: 1 XRD = 1 vote, leaving out the {n} addresses with the most XRD. It shows whether the result hinges on a few wallets.
no_whales.attack: Whales dodge the exclusion by splitting their XRD into addresses smaller than the ten largest. It takes capital.

whales_only.name: Large wallets only
whales_only.rule: 1 XRD = 1 vote, but only addresses holding {whale} XRD or more count. It shows what the whales alone would have decided.
whales_only.attack: Only addresses holding {whale} XRD or more count; splitting gains nothing. It takes a lot of capital, though very few people decide.

tips.col_method: The rule deciding how much each vote weighs
tips.col_result: What this method would have decided, with the vote's quorum and approval threshold
tips.col_support: Weight in favour over weight in favour and against (abstentions left out). The vertical line marks the approval threshold
tips.col_overlap: How many of the elected seats under this method match the council elected by 1 XRD = 1 vote
tips.fact_seats: Number of seats elected in this Majority Judgment election
tips.col_counted: Addresses whose vote counts under this method; the rest are left out for not meeting its requirements
tips.col_nakamoto: The number is the fewest addresses that together hold more than half of the weight (Nakamoto coefficient). The level and the bar are the degree of decentralisation: effective voters over voters, 100 % when all weigh the same
tips.col_decisive: How many addresses on the winning side, heaviest first, would have been enough on their own to decide the vote, even if everyone else voted the other way
tips.outcome_approved: There is quorum and the vote in favour passes the approval threshold
tips.outcome_rejected: There is quorum, but the vote in favour does not reach the approval threshold
tips.outcome_no_quorum: The XRD of the addresses that count under this method fall short of the quorum, so the result would not be valid
tips.outcome_winner: The option with the most weight under this method
tips.outcome_none: No address meets this method's requirements
tips.support: {pct} in favour; at least {threshold} is needed
tips.nakamoto: {n} of {of} addresses ({share}) hold more than half of the weight. Degree of decentralisation: {spread}, as they amount to {eff} effective voters out of {of}: {level}
tips.counted: {n} addresses count; {out} are left out under this method
tips.decisive: The {count} largest of {of} addresses on the winning side, holding {xrd} XRD, were enough to decide it
tips.badge_current: The method votes use today: the others are compared with it
tips.badge_changes: Under this method the result would have differed from the current one
tips.badge_same: Under this method the result would have been the same as the current one
tips.conc_top1: The heaviest address holds {pct} of the vote
tips.conc_top10: The next 9 heaviest addresses hold {pct} of the vote
tips.conc_rest: All other addresses together hold {pct} of the vote
tips.detail_counted: Addresses whose vote counts under this method, and how many are left out
tips.detail_effective: Effective voters: {n} of {of}. It is the number of equally sized addresses that would share power the same way. If {of} addresses vote but amount to {n}, in practice about {n} wallets decide. It is 1 over the sum of each address's squared share of the weight (Herfindahl index). If all weighed the same it would be {of}
tips.detail_quorum: XRD of the addresses that count, against the minimum the vote needs for the result to be valid
tips.kpi_consensus: How many alternative methods would have given the same result as 1 XRD = 1 vote
tips.kpi_current: Under the current method, the fewest addresses that together hold more than half of the vote
tips.kpi_most_spread: The method with the highest degree of decentralisation
tips.kpi_most_concentrated: The method with the lowest degree of decentralisation: power sits in the fewest hands
tips.level_extreme: A single address holds more than half of the weight and decides alone, however many others vote
tips.level_high: Decentralisation below 15 %: power amounts to very few addresses
tips.detail_spread: Effective voters over voters (Simpson evenness). 100 % when every address weighs the same; the lower, the more weight sits with a few
tips.level_minimal: Decentralisation of 65 % or more: the weight is close to evenly shared
tips.col_resistance: Resistance to manipulation: how hard it is for one person to weigh more than their share. With no KYC, creating addresses and splitting XRD between them is free. Very low: gamed at almost no cost. High: weight only comes from buying XRD. Hover each method to see how it is gamed and what it would take to turn this vote around
tips.resistance_very_low: One person can multiply their vote by creating many addresses, at almost no cost
tips.resistance_low: Each extra vote is cheap, or the method's safeguard (a cap, an exclusion) is dodged for free by splitting the XRD across addresses
tips.resistance_medium: Gaming it takes accounts prepared long in advance, or it only works to block the result
tips.resistance_high: Splitting into addresses adds no votes: the only way to weigh more is to hold more XRD
tips.kpi_balanced: The method that best combines resistance to manipulation and decentralisation (geometric mean of both): hard to game and with power spread out. 100 % decentralisation means every address weighs the same
tips.kpi_unbalanced: The method that combines them worst: it fails at one of the two at least. A 100 % decentralised method (every address weighs the same) that can be gamed for free by creating addresses is not balanced
tips.fact_voters: Addresses with > 0 XRD voting power counted in the comparison
tips.fact_voters_with_zero: {counted} of {total} addresses with > 0 XRD voting power at the snapshot ({zero} voted with 0 XRD and are excluded from the comparison)
tips.fact_xrd: Total voting power of those addresses under the current method
tips.fact_quorum: XRD that must take part for the result to be valid
tips.fact_threshold: Share of the vote in favour needed to pass
tips.counted_share: {pct} of the addresses that voted count under this method ({n} of {of}); the rest do not meet its requirements
tips.decisive_share: {pct} of the addresses on the winning side ({n} of {of}), heaviest first, were enough to decide the result even if everyone else voted the other way
tips.fact_option: {n} addresses voted "{label}" ({pct} of those who voted)
tips.threshold_mark: Approval threshold: at least {pct} in favour is needed to pass. It is the vertical line on the bar
tips.kpi_effective: Method with the best combination of manipulation resistance, decentralisation, and quorum reached in this vote
tips.kpi_ineffective: Method with the worst combination of manipulation resistance, decentralisation, and quorum reached in this vote

resistance_hints.very_low: votes multiply by creating addresses, almost for free
resistance_hints.low: extra votes are cheap or the safeguard is dodged by splitting
resistance_hints.medium: takes accounts prepared years ahead, or only works to block
resistance_hints.high: splitting gains nothing: only more XRD adds weight

compare.cost_addresses: To turn this vote around, {addresses} new addresses holding {each} XRD each would do ({xrd} XRD in total).
compare.cost_addresses_aged: To turn it around it would take {addresses} accounts at least {years} old holding {each} XRD each ({xrd} XRD in total). New accounts do not count.
compare.cost_capital: To turn it around it would take {xrd} more XRD ({pct} of what already voted).
compare.cost_capital_split: To turn it around it would take {xrd} more XRD ({pct} of what already voted), split across {addresses} addresses to dodge the cap.
compare.cost_capital_aged: To turn it around it would take {xrd} more XRD ({pct} of what already voted) held in an account at least {years} old; an old account with freshly bought XRD will do.
compare.cost_capital_split_aged: To turn it around it would take {xrd} more XRD ({pct} of what already voted), split across {addresses} accounts at least {years} old to dodge the cap.
compare.cost_impossible: Adding votes cannot turn this result around.
compare.cost_none: There is no clear result to turn around (no quorum or no valid votes).
compare.g_resistance: How hard it is for one person to weigh more than their share. With no KYC, new addresses are free and so is splitting XRD between them, so methods that count addresses or favour small balances are easy to game. Each method's details price turning this vote around.
compare.kpi_balance_hint: {resistance} resistance · {n} of {of} addresses needed for half of the vote ({pct} decentralisation)
